Now I'm shaping the head, positioning it toward the front and giving it a broad, round profile with a short muzzle typical of a red panda's face.

Adding cheek fluffs, muzzle, nose, and eyes...

Now I'm layering in the darker eye patches with angled tear-mark stripes running to the mouth, plus white eyebrow spots and cream forehead markings, keeping the crown a rustier tone than the rest of the face. Next I'm starting on the large triangular ears.

For the rings I'll alternate rust and darker russet tones with a dark tip, tapering the thickness from thicker at the base to thinner near the tip, curving the tail path upward and back from the rump.

Planning the tail geometry with a smooth curve staying above the floor, built from low-poly cylinder segments oriented along the curve's tangent with alternating ring colors for the bushy look.

Now I'm adding smaller details for extra polish: fur tufts on cheeks and tail edges, white chin fluff, toe claws, and considering subtle noise texture on the fur material for realism.

Just the model itself, no ground plane—I'll keep a neutral, readable rest pose with the head facing forward and slightly up. I'm setting up helper functions: a cached material creator, a seeded RNG, an ellipsoid-mesh helper that scales and positions a shared low-poly sphere geometry, so I can build the whole figure efficiently without duplicating geometry data.

Now I'm planning the overall scene budget and hierarchy—using a Group structure for root, body, head (pivoted at the neck), tail, and legs—then working out real-world proportions, setting the body center height and radius so the back, belly, and legs read correctly for a red panda's short-legged stance.

I'm positioning the head relative to the body, checking overlap at the neck, and calculating the total height to ears (~0.38m) and overall body-plus-tail length (~1.1m), comparing against realistic red panda measurements before considering enlarging the head slightly for a stylized, cuter look.

For the body shape, I'm using low-poly faceted spheres to get a blocky, puppet-like aesthetic rather than smooth geometry, scaling them to form the torso, chest, and shoulders with rust coloring.

Next I'm adding a dark-brown chest patch, a rump sphere positioned slightly higher and further back, and a darker belly ellipsoid, thinking about whether to include a subtler dorsal ridge for the back coloring.

Placing shoulder spheres...

Adding the hock connecting knee to heel for a plantigrade hind leg, then moving to head details — placing the head group with a slight upward pitch and defining the skull shape with rust coloring, considering a lighter ochre tone for the forehead area typical of red pandas.

Now I'm adding facial fluff: white cheek puffs as scaled spheres, plus small white cone-shaped tufts pointing outward and down from each cheek, using a direction-based helper to orient the cones properly. Moving on to the white muzzle next.

Still placing muzzle geometry...
